what: evidence that the atlas face has been mounted in a real, non-headless window -- not only in the headless renderer tools/shoot.mjs and tools/browser-mount-smoke.mjs drive
why: req/02 W15 clause 3: a face must carry proof of having mounted in a real window a person could look at. tools/browser-mount-smoke.mjs and tools/real-window-smoke.mjs in this same faces/atlas/tools/ directory were written from zero for this face, following the same shape faces/ledger, faces/notice, faces/held, faces/receipt and faces/graph already established (fixture served over http + shell/tools/real_window.ps1, the shell's own real-window instrument, reused rather than duplicated).
how: tools/real-window-smoke.mjs starts a static file server rooted at the repo (answering /s-common/tokens.css from tokens/tokens.css, the one in-repo stylesheet of record), then shells out to shell/tools/real_window.ps1 with the fixture's URL. That script opens Chrome in app mode at 1440x900, waits, reads the window's own title back through the Win32 window list, and screenshots the window's own visible bounds (this lane's own fix: DwmGetWindowAttribute(DWMWA_EXTENDED_FRAME_BOUNDS), not the legacy GetWindowRect -- see capture_bleed_fix below). This face's mount fixture (fixtures/browser-mount-entry.mjs + fixtures/browser-mount.html) imports index.mjs directly and calls mount(host, stubPort, []) against a folded list envelope of three transformations spelled out inline in the fixture -- two paths, one touched twice (deck.pdf) and one touched once (budget.xlsx, drawn as a subject here even though faces/graph would not draw it at all). The entry script writes the element/subject counts into document.title so the numbers below are the numbers the page itself computed, not typed by hand.
colour_status: RESOLVED. This face reuses the tokens self-ownership atom faces/receipt's lane already landed (tokens/tokens.css, in-repo, no dependency on any retired tree) -- both real-window captures below show the derived palette actually applied (light page / dark page, read by eye in the pictures and corroborated by tools/shoot.mjs's own tokensResolved reading), not a placeholder colour.
capture_bleed_fix: Owner eye-judgment correction (2026-08-25): shell/tools/real_window.ps1's own captures were bleeding a sliver of whatever sat behind the window at its edges. Root cause: GetWindowRect on modern Windows includes several pixels of invisible DWM resize/drop-shadow border outside the window's actual painted content, and CopyFromScreen against that rect copies those pixels too. Fixed in shell/tools/real_window.ps1 (this lane, patched in place, not duplicated) by reading DwmGetWindowAttribute(DWMWA_EXTENDED_FRAME_BOUNDS) instead, with GetWindowRect kept as a fallback if the DWM call fails. Evidence this actually took effect on this run: the captured rect below (47,40 1426x893) is narrower than the requested --window-size=1440,900 at --window-position=40,40 -- the legacy GetWindowRect path would have reported a rect at or slightly larger than the requested window size (the invisible border adds to it, not subtracts), so a rect smaller than the request is direct, measured evidence the DWM path ran, not merely a code-level claim.
